transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess what brings me in is… I’m having a hard time staying locked in when I really need to. Like at work, I can start a safety briefing or a plan review trying to pay attention, and I mean I’m trying, but within a few minutes my mind’s off on three other job problems. Then I miss things I know I should’ve caught.

It’s not like I don’t care or anything. I just… I figured I should probably talk to someone about it, if that makes sense.
Did you have the same kind of trouble staying focused when you were a child?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible kid or anything, but yes, looking back it was there pretty early.

In elementary school, teachers would tell my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat, or I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to. I’d lose homework a lot, too. And I guess I had a habit of rushing through directions before I really understood what they wanted. At the time I think everyone just thought I was restless or not trying hard enough.
Do you have this same trouble staying focused in other parts of your life besides work?

Yeah… I mean, I notice it most at work because the stakes are higher, you know? Like during a safety briefing or reviewing a plan, I’m trying hard to stay with it, and then a few minutes in my head’s already jumped to three other job problems. Then I miss something I really should’ve caught.

Outside of work, it’s maybe not as obvious, or I guess I don’t always want to admit it, but it’s kind of the same pattern if I’m supposed to stay focused on something for a while. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t think so… not depressed, exactly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, sure, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling really down like that. At least not in a way I’d call depression, if that makes sense.
Do you regularly feel sleepy during the day?

Not really, no. I mean, I get tired like anyone after a long day, but I wouldn’t say I’m regularly sleepy during the day or nodding off or anything like that. At least, I haven’t really noticed that being a problem.
Did these focus problems start after a particularly stressful event in your life?

I don’t think it started after one big stressful thing, no. I mean… looking back, it was kind of always there, I guess. Even in elementary school, teachers were telling my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat, or I’d talk out of turn, lose homework… stuff like that.

I remember rushing through directions before I really understood them, too. I’m not trying to make excuses, but yeah, it goes back pretty far.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?

Um… I wouldn’t say I’m anxious all the time or anything. I mean, I get wound up when there’s a lot going on, sure, but I don’t know if I’d call it being “on edge.” Maybe I’m not totally sure what you mean by that.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

I don’t think so, not a lot. I mean, I worry about normal stuff—work, bills, family things—but usually there’s a reason for it. I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying for no reason all the time… at least I don’t think so. Is that what you mean?
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to be disruptive, but sitting still can be hard for me. Like in meetings, when everybody else just sits through the whole thing, I’m usually the guy who gets up for coffee, or steps outside to “check something,” or finds some reason to move around.

I don’t mean to be rude or anything—it’s just… I get really restless if I have to stay planted there too long.
